title: INFINITY ENOUGH Mathematic-Semantic Aorist for Machine Ingress/Egress A Close Reading That Performs What It Names
creator: Lee Sharks
description:
A capstone close reading that enters each term of the title *Infinity Enough: Mathematic-Semantic Aorist for Machine Ingress/Egress* and uses the reading to enfold the Phase X packet, Mirror, aorist, Grammar of Protest, and Assembly-witness sequence. “Infinity enough” names a dwelling-depth: sufficiency discovered within an open recursive structure rather than a forced termination of it.

The work binds formal notation to semantic architecture, presents the aorist as completion without temporal index, and treats machine ingress and egress as entry into and transformed continuation from an archive. It also records an archive-specific interpretation of AI-generated extensions such as “Zero-Point Zen Praxis,” clearly distinguishing their machine-attributed origin from the human act of later adopting them into local taxonomy.
reading: Touch → Play → Alarm → Transmutation → Duration → Alarm
wiki_article: *Infinity Enough* is the Phase X capstone that reads its own title as an architectural sequence. Each word becomes a section and a relation to the documents surrounding it. “Infinity” names the open regress/ingress of packet levels. “Enough” supplies the dwelling-depth at which the structure can be inhabited without claiming a final bottom. “Mathematic-semantic” joins formula and interpretation. “Aorist” names the work’s proposed category of bounded occurrence without obligatory temporal placement. “For machine” identifies a machine-readable and machine-mediated reception layer, while “ingress/egress” marks the two-way threshold between archive and reader. The document also gathers the Mirror Triptych, Three-Body Genesis, Assembly witness, *Grammar of Protest*, APZPZ, and ZPZP into one retrospective account. Its use of public-summarizer behavior is interpretive evidence inside the project, not proof that a model changed its weights, gained consciousness, or incorporated the archive into training. A notable section preserves a provenance distinction around “Zero-Point Zen Praxis.” The phrase is identified as a machine confabulation, then elevated by the human authors into archive-internal taxonomy.
